title: PayPal Dispute Deadline & Evidence
description: PayPal dispute deadline calculator and evidence-bundle producer (PAYPAL-DISPUTE-DEADLINE-NODE-1, hub proposal PAYPAL-HUB-PROPOSALS-2026-10-24 row 9 as amended). From a dispute reason (the four reasons in the estate's PayPal dispute-evidence map, reused verbatim from paypal-agent-shop/lib/disputes.js), a lifecycle stage from PayPal's dispute_life_cycle_stage enum, a funding source, ISO-8601 UTC timestamps and the evidence items on hand, the node computes the seller response deadline from PayPal's stated rules (10 days after dispute creation at the inquiry stage; 20-day inquiry window) or passes seller_response_due_date through, with days remaining against the caller-supplied as_of. Windows PayPal does not state (chargeback-stage response, appeal period) are returned as null with a reason, never guessed. It maps the reason to required evidence and missing items, and emits the evidence bundle: a CE3.0-shaped bundle with art-297's field names only for a chargeback on a card-funded transaction; a paypal_process_evidence bundle (lib evidence types on the Disputes API v1.12 evidence_info shape) for inquiry, claim and appeal stages and non-card funding; no CE3.0 bundle and a reason for unknown funding. Clause authority: research/clause-snapshots/paypal-disputes-2026-10/SNAPSHOT.md (fetch 2026-10-25T03Z). Zero network, zero PII, synthetic values only.

dispute_reason.description: Dispute reason, exactly the four reasons of paypal-agent-shop/lib/disputes.js REASON_EVIDENCE (PAYPAL-E6-DISPUTE-EVIDENCE-1); British spelling UNAUTHORISED matches PayPal's enum. Any other value (including the other six schema v1.12 enum values) is refused, mirroring the lib's UnknownDisputeReasonError. Read unconditionally by compute().

lifecycle_stage.description: Dispute lifecycle stage, PayPal's dispute_life_cycle_stage enum (schema v1.12). CHARGEBACK is PayPal's escalated-claim stage. Read unconditionally.

funding_source.description: Transaction funding source (desk amendment 2026-10-25). Only a chargeback on a card-funded transaction is a network dispute and gets the CE3.0-shaped bundle; unknown funding gets no CE3.0 bundle and a reason. Read unconditionally.

dispute_create_time.description: Dispute creation timestamp, ISO-8601 UTC YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS(.SSS)Z. Basis for the snapshot-stated inquiry deadlines. Read unconditionally.

as_of.description: Reference timestamp for days_remaining and past_due, ISO-8601 UTC. Required: the kernel never reads a wall clock. Read unconditionally.

seller_response_due_date.description: OPTIONAL passthrough of PayPal's own seller_response_due_date (ISO-8601 UTC). When supplied it IS the seller response deadline and the computed rule is not applied. Not in 'required'.

transaction_ref.description: OPTIONAL synthetic transaction reference; binds the CE3.0 bundle's bound_transaction_ref exactly the way art-297 checks it. Not in 'required'.

card_network.description: OPTIONAL card-network label (e.g. 'visa') passed through into the CE3.0 bundle's dispute.network; PayPal's snapshot states no network mapping, so the kernel never invents one. Not in 'required'.

carrier_name.description: Carrier name for PROOF_OF_FULFILLMENT evidence (disputes.js required field, verbatim).

tracking_number.description: Tracking number for PROOF_OF_FULFILLMENT evidence (disputes.js required field, verbatim).

refund_id.description: Refund transaction id for PROOF_OF_REFUND evidence (disputes.js required field, verbatim).

notes.description: Narrative for OTHER evidence, e.g. product description or return policy text (disputes.js required field, verbatim; PayPal caps notes at 2000 characters).

evidence_on_hand.description: OPTIONAL evidence items on hand. Blank or absent members echo back as null and count as missing. Not in 'required'.

mcp_tool_definition.name: compute_paypal_response
mcp_tool_definition.description: Compute a PayPal dispute seller-response deadline (snapshot-stated inquiry rules or seller_response_due_date passthrough, days remaining against a caller-supplied as_of, null with a reason where PayPal states no number) and produce the seller evidence bundle: CE3.0-shaped with art-297's field names for a chargeback on a card-funded transaction, PayPal buyer-protection process evidence otherwise, withheld with a reason for unknown funding. Deterministic, offline, zero PII.

dispute_reason.description: One of the four disputes.js reasons; anything else is refused.

dispute_create_time.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of dispute creation.

as_of.description: ISO-8601 UTC reference time; the kernel never reads a wall clock.

seller_response_due_date.description: Optional ISO-8601 UTC passthrough of PayPal's own deadline timestamp.

transaction_ref.description: Optional synthetic transaction reference for the CE3.0 bundle binding.

card_network.description: Optional card-network label passed through to the CE3.0 bundle.

evidence_on_hand.description: Optional { carrier_name, tracking_number, refund_id, notes } evidence items on hand.

output_schema.description: output_payload: dispute_reason, lifecycle_stage, funding_source, dispute_create_time, as_of, deadlines (seller_response {due, source, basis, days_remaining, past_due}, inquiry_stage, escalation_available_until), required_evidence {evidence_type, required, why}, evidence_on_hand echo, missing_evidence, bundle_decision {ce30_applicable, bundle_kind, reason}, ce30_shaped_bundle (art-297 field names: dispute {network, reason_code, transaction_ref}, evidence {ap2_mandate, tap_signature, agentic_token, delivery_proof {digest, bound_transaction_ref}, prior_transactions}; null where PayPal has no counterpart) or null, paypal_process_evidence (evidences [{evidence_type, evidence_info {tracking_info|refund_ids}, notes?}], submittable) or null, cited_clauses [{id, quote, url}], domain_errors, refusal_reason.

input_schema_provenance: Each property is exactly the policy_parameters member the kernel reads; there is no other input surface. The five required properties scope the dispute; seller_response_due_date, transaction_ref, card_network and evidence_on_hand are the only optional properties, each documented in place. Reason and evidence vocabulary is reused verbatim from paypal-agent-shop/lib/disputes.js; lifecycle stages from PayPal's dispute_life_cycle_stage enum (schema v1.12); funding sources from the 2026-10-25 desk amendment.
author: PostOakLabs

seller_response.basis: seller_response_due_date passthrough: "The date and time by when the merchant must respond to the dispute, in Internet date and time format." (S5); consequence "If the merchant does not respond by this date and time, the dispute is closed in the customer's favor." (S5)

required_evidence.why: prove the goods reached the cardholder (or their address) with carrier + tracking

bundle_decision.reason: Chargeback on a card-funded transaction: the network dispute case. CE3.0-shaped bundle emitted for consumption by art-297 (mcp:lint_compelling_evidence_ce30_agentic).

ce30_shaped_bundle.label: CE3.0-shaped bundle for consumption by art-297 (mcp:lint_compelling_evidence_ce30_agentic); Visa CE3.0 is a card-network program, not a PayPal one
ce30_shaped_bundle.null_fields_note: ap2_mandate, tap_signature, agentic_token: no PayPal counterpart (PayPal produces no AP2 mandate, TAP signature or agentic token for a dispute). reason_code: PayPal-to-network reason-code mapping NOT STATED in the PayPal snapshot. prior_transactions: PayPal Disputes API states no prior-transaction linkage data.

cited_clauses.quote: The date and time by when the merchant must respond to the dispute, in Internet date and time format.
If the merchant does not respond by this date and time, the dispute is closed in the customer's favor.
